hints.text: Which function has derivative $\frac{1}{x}$? Think about the logarithm functions you know.
An antiderivative is $F(x) = \ln x$. Evaluate it at the two limits and compute $F(e) - F(1)$.
The value is $\ln e - \ln 1 = 1 - 0 = 1$, so the integral equals $1$.

explanation: An antiderivative of $\frac{1}{x}$ (for $x > 0$) is the natural logarithm $\ln x$.
By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $\int_1^e \frac{1}{x} \, dx = \ln e - \ln 1$.
This is $1 - 0 = 1$. In fact this is one way to define $e$: the number that makes the area under $\frac{1}{x}$ from $1$ equal to exactly $1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Power rule trap
steps: Trying the power rule on $x^{-1}$ gives $\frac{x^0}{0}$ — division by zero. The power rule fails exactly at $n = -1$.
That gap is filled by the logarithm: $\frac{d}{dx} \ln x = \frac{1}{x}$.
